chunks: Al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad al-Jawharī narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:

I asked him about a man who anoints himself with an oil containing fragrance while intending to enter ihram. He said: “Do not anoint yourself, when you intend to enter ihram, with oil containing musk or ambergris whose scent remains in your head after you enter ihram. Anoint yourself with whatever oil you wish when you intend to enter ihram, before the ghusl and after it; but once you have entered ihram, oil has become forbidden for you until you exit ihram.”

key_terms.تُحِلَّ: to exit the state of ihram and become lawful again
key_terms.طِيبٌ: fragrance or perfume in the oil
key_terms.يُحْرِمَ: to enter the state of ihram
key_terms.ٱلْغُسْلِ: the ritual bath taken in preparation

ai.seo_question: Can a person use scented or unscented oil before entering ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a legal ruling related to preparing for ihram. It forbids using scented oil whose fragrance remains after entering ihram, while allowing other oils before ihram, and it states that oil becomes forbidden after ihram begins until one exits it.
